intelligence.human_view: Think of a host who greets you at the door, then steps aside so you can come in — that is the banner, and that is the whole page. Everything in this group follows the same courtesy: the welcome does not stand in the doorway, the score does not turn the meeting place into a scoreboard, the diamond does not pretend to be real when it disappears, the connection does not make you press a button before you may speak. What the page can do, it shows — four buttons in the row, the footer at the bottom of every post, the gauge in paint where the eye can see it. And what the machine claims, it proves — filed is not live, a byte check is not a live check, one lucky green probe is not a fix. The signature piece is the same law at its most beautiful: a thing that changes with the day and is judged by the eye, not by the brief. A page built this way never has to announce itself. It greets, it shows, it proves, and it gets out of the way.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a kind host at the door. She says good morning. Then she steps aside so you can come in and play. She does not stand in the doorway all day. That is the banner. The buttons you need are right in front of you. You can see them. So you can use them. If you want to be friends, you just say hello. The hello is the asking. If they answer, that is a yes. If they do not answer, that is a no. No big button needed. The shiny things must look real. If a diamond just fades away, it is not a real diamond. Make something real instead, like a spinning ball. And always check the real page, not just the paper. The real page shows what is really there.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, the whole night comes down to good manners, dear. The banner says good morning and then folds itself away, so you can get on with your day. The buttons sit right where you can see them, dear — message, mail, audio, video — because if you cannot see what you can do, you never do it. To connect with someone, you just say hello, dear — the hello is the asking, and their answer is the yes. The shiny things must look real, dear, not glow so bright you cannot see them, and a diamond that disappears is no diamond at all. And we check the real page, dear, not just the paper — because the real page shows what is really there.
intelligence.naya_view: THE PAGE GETS OUT OF ITS OWN WAY. THE BANNER FOLDS AWAY ON ITS OWN — GOOD MORNING, THEN GONE. SHOW WHAT THE PAGE CAN DO, IN THE ROW, WHERE THE EYE ALREADY IS. SEND IS THE REQUEST — A REPLY IS YES, SILENCE IS NO. REAL OR REPLACED. FILED IS NOT LIVE. VERIFY LIVE, NOT ONLY IN BYTES. CAUSE FIRST, THEN RETRY.
